post.title: How one late payment can trigger a 29.99% penalty APR
post.ig:
One late payment can trigger a 29.99% rate.

It's called a penalty APR. Chase card terms in 2026 list it at up to 29.99%.
Under the CARD Act and Regulation Z, new purchases can get the higher rate after a 45-day notice; your existing balance is protected unless you're more than 60 days late.
Our math: on a $6,000 balance, monthly interest goes from $105 at 21% to $149.95 at 29.99%, or $269.70 extra over six months if the balance stays flat.
After six on-time minimum payments in a row, the issuer must drop the penalty rate on that old balance. A court vacated the CFPB's $8 late fee rule in April 2025.

Sources: 12 CFR 1026.55 and 1026.9 (Regulation Z), Credit CARD Act, Chase pricing terms (2026), U.S. District Court N.D. Texas (April 2025).
